title: Confidence-gated prefill & rollback controller for speculative decode
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: implement a confidence-gated prefill controller that can accept tentative early outputs from a fast speculative model and either commit them or roll back to a slower, higher-quality path when confidence falls below thresholds. The controller must coordinate with kernel selection and attention budget signals to avoid triggering expensive fallbacks unnecessarily and should expose telemetry for acceptance rate, rollback frequency, and end-to-end P90 latency.

Scope: runtime-side controller + light operator hooks. Does not include new model training or changes to model scoring functions. Work includes: probe scheduling during prefill, confidence aggregator, kernel-affinity hinting to preference cheaper kernels for speculative paths, rollback orchestration (kv cache invalidation/replay), and rollout policy for gradual activation.

Non-goals: changing model architectures, full eval harness for every workload (we will reuse existing eval sets), making changes to public API surface.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Controller can mark speculative prefill outputs as accepted or rejected based on a configurable confidence score and two-stage thresholds.
2) When rejected, controller triggers deterministic rollback: invalidates speculative KV segments for that request and dispatches decode to the fallback model without user-visible duplication of tokens.
3) Integration tests show <2% incidence of user-visible token duplication on synthetic workload and rollback latency <= 60ms median added on fallback paths.
4) Telemetry dashboard surfaces acceptance_rate, rollback_rate_by_model, rollback_latency_histogram, kernel_affinity_use, and downstream latency impact.
5) Canary rollout (5% traffic) runs for 48 hours with no P1 regressions before 25% and then 100% rollout steps.
implementation_notes:
Design: controller maintains a short-lived 'prefill probe window' during which the speculative model's softmax-derived confidence + alignment heuristics are aggregated. Confidence aggregator includes: token-level max-prob, entropy, repetition penalty signals, and a small learned logistic calibrator (runtime table) per model family.

Kernel selection interaction: speculative path will hint 'low-latency kernels' (e.g., int8 kernels with fused attention) via kernel_affinity header. If the controller detects repeated rollbacks from a kernel-affinity group, it will deprioritize that kernel for the model-family for a transient period.

KV cache handling: when speculative output is accepted, the speculative KV segment is merged into the session's canonical KV in a single atomic step. When rejected, the segment is discarded and any downstream decoder state is recreated by replaying canonical inputs on the fallback model. To keep replay cost bounded, we limit probes to N tokens (configurable, default 8).

Fallback orchestration: fallback model selection favors kernel-compatible variants with higher quality (e.g., same model quantized to fp16 or a larger family member). Controller will attempt 'soft re-decoding' by replaying only the last M tokens to rehydrate KV cache when possible.

Config knobs: probe_window_tokens, accept_threshold, reject_threshold, max_probe_tokens, kernel_affinity_timeout_sec, fallback_model_map (map of speculative->fallback families).
test_plan:
Unit tests for confidence aggregator and kernel hint toggles. Integration tests simulate mixed workloads: short-chat (<=64 tokens), long-dialog (>=512 tokens), and embeddings-triggered prefill. Load test: synthetic 5000 rps with mixed sequence lengths to measure rollback_rate and tail latency. Chaos: inject artificial kernel slowdowns and verify controller moves traffic to fallback without violating SLO.

Validation: A/B compare baseline: acceptance_rate and token-cost-per-response; expect >8% token-cost reduction on optimistic workloads while keeping quality regression <0.5% on eval prompts.

E2E: deploy canary in dedicated pool, run 48h synthetic + 24h seeded customer traffic sample (with consent) before wider rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal QA in sandbox with 0.1% traffic. 2) Canary: 5% of traffic, monitor telemetry for 48h. 3) Ramp: 25% for 24h, 50% for 24h, 100% if no regressions. 4) Emergency kill: controller has an exposure circuit breaker based on rollback_rate (>5% sustained) or user_duplication (>0.2%): instant disable and fall back to pre-controller routing. 5) Postmortem window: daily review during ramp, then weekly for 4 weeks.

2025-02-12 - Review (Marcelo Ortega): kernel-affinity timeout feels heuristical; suggest switch to exponentially-weighted penalty with tunable decay. Action: implement ewma-based penalty (in progress).
2025-02-14 - Design feedback (Product): add explicit operator flag to disable speculative commits for customers using strict audit trails. Added config operator:disable_speculative_commits.
2025-02-16 - Engineering note: KV replay optimized by sending a compacted token delta; reduces replay time by ~28% in initial runs. Patch linked in PR #1428.
2025-02-18 - QA: Integration load test reached 5k rps; rollback_rate at 1.1% overall, rollback_latency_p90 = 58ms. Preparing canary manifests for dedicated pool.
